title: History 15: The size era: FP8, GGUF and 4-bit formats arrive

questions.q: According to the lesson, what is the primary trade-off made when using lower-bit formats like FP8, GGUF, or 4-bit integers?
options: Trading a tiny amount of precision for a massive amount of capacity
Trading model speed for higher accuracy
Trading storage space for increased model complexity
Trading hardware compatibility for better visual output
questions.answer: Trading a tiny amount of precision for a massive amount of capacity
questions.why: The 'Why this matters' section explicitly states: 'We are trading a tiny amount of precision for a massive amount of capacity.'

questions.q: In the provided lab results, what was the calculated Mean Absolute Error (MAE) for the INT4 quantization?
questions.why: The 'Lab' section lists the exact result: `RESULT int4_error = 0.125481`.

questions.q: What specific behavior does the `comfy_quant` module exhibit if a GPU does not support INT8 compute, as described in the 'In ComfyUI' section?
questions.answer: It quietly reverts to full precision to ensure stability and prevent crashes.
questions.why: The text states: 'The test... ensures that if your GPU doesn't support INT8 compute, ComfyUI doesn't crash. It quietly reverts to full precision.'

questions.q: Based on the lab analysis, why are 4-bit models often described as requiring 'smoothing' or 'calibration' techniques, whereas 8-bit models are often 'drop-in' replacements?
options: Because 4-bit models use a coarser grid, resulting in an error roughly 18 times larger than INT8
Because 4-bit models require more VRAM than 8-bit models
Because 8-bit models cannot be loaded into standard PyTorch modules
Because 4-bit models are incompatible with the GGUF format
questions.answer: Because 4-bit models use a coarser grid, resulting in an error roughly 18 times larger than INT8
questions.why: The 'Lab' section notes that the INT4 error is 'roughly 18 times larger' than the INT8 error and concludes: 'This mathematical reality is why 4-bit models often require "smoothing" or "calibration" techniques... whereas 8-bit models are often "drop-in" replacements.'

questions.q: According to the 'Common mistakes' section, what is a key reason not to judge a quantization format solely by its bit count?
questions.answer: Because sophisticated formats like GGUF Q4_K_M use block-wise scaling and outlier handling, making them better than naive quantization of the same bit count.
questions.why: The text states: 'Don't judge a format by its bit count alone; judge it by its quantization algorithm,' citing that modern formats use 'block-wise scaling and outlier handling' which makes them superior to naive rounding.
